verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes ticket-weighted eligibility, where additional tickets increase an affiliate's chances of winning.
The client defines separate Small and Big Block ticket counters, per-referral issuance, draw eligibility windows, post-draw resets, and exclusion of secondary sales from ticket creation.
The FAQ establishes active-ticket transfer with NFT ownership and ticket allocation to an existing holder when a mint has no referral code.
Eliminating Big Blocks changes the software to maintain only the Small Block ticket counter and removes the obsolete Big Block eligibility and reset rules.
The client defines one ticket per successful referral for the current 100-sale draw and requires those tickets to expire after that draw.
The client requires both absent and invalid referral codes to generate a ticket for a randomly selected existing NFT holder.
First concrete failure of the no-referral USDC path: the completed mint generated no prize ticket.
The client explicitly leaves undecided whether a no-referral primary mint must generate a ticket, creating material uncertainty in ticket issuance behavior.
Target-specific implementation claim after the first failure: the freelancer reports that no-referral mints now generate a ticket.

value_updates.prize_entry_unit: One Small Block ticket generated per successful primary mint

verdicts.decision_note: The client requires one ticket per primary mint, including random allocation when no valid referral is used; the source does not modify the existing current-draw eligibility window.
The client resolves the prior uncertainty by requiring tickets for primary mints while excluding secondary-market sales.
Post-fix persistence with a new technical finding: no-referral tickets are not awarded unless the separate random-referral follow-up transaction executes.
The client accepts an executable first-mint exception because no earlier NFT exists to receive that mint's ticket.
Target-specific implementation claim after the follow-up-transaction failure: the freelancer reports ticket issuance for both code-used and finalized no-code paths.
First concrete verification of the mobile no-referral path after the implementation claim; the client reports that the requested ticket-and-commission test worked perfectly.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
yes, the USDC minting was successful, and my #4 mint now has $5 and a ticket.

but when we mint without using a referral code, there seems to be no ticket generated, and no ticket and commission given out at random

execution.observed_behavior: A USDC mint using a referral code successfully awarded a ticket to NFT #4.
